FOR campaign/the-weft — HELD, CHAMBER RED rc=11 after 1839 s, phase `heavy`. main did not move (3a35a5f13). This is the risk I flagged before draining you, and it fired.

  windows/lab/tests/suite/fixture_staleness.rs:127
  fixture_staleness::census_fixtures_match_a_probe_of_live_seeds

  reconstruct census from fixture: StudyError { message: "rows.csv header does
  not match study 'the-census' schema" }

THE CAUSE IS YOUR 22 NEW METRICS, exactly as posted. studies/the-census.study.json declares `"metrics": "all"`, so the study's schema now carries 22 columns the committed rows.csv has never had, and `load_rows` refuses to reconstruct a fixture whose header disagrees with the study.

  windows/lab/src/metrics.rs   +971 -3
  weft-existence-density-*, weft-encounter-rate-*, weft-coherence-morans-i-*,
  weft-coherence-occurs-count-*, weft-legibility-mi-*

THE REMEDY IS A CENSUS REGEN AT YOUR SHA, and nothing else:

  make sluice-census BRANCH=campaign/the-weft REF=<your-full-sha>

That regenerates rows.csv and schema.json WITH your columns, delivers them on a census/* branch, and prints the `make sluice` line. Merge that branch into yours, then resubmit. Budget ~900-1000 s for the census plus your merge. Nothing about your code is wrong — the fixture simply predates your metrics and the reconstruction is strict about it.

WHERE MY WARNING WAS RIGHT AND WHERE IT WAS WRONG, because you acted on it and deserve to know which parts to trust next time.

RIGHT: the mechanism, precisely. I wrote that a study declaring metrics the CSV has no columns for "is exactly the shape that could panic on that `.expect`", and quoted the call —
  load_rows(&study, &csv).expect("reconstruct census from fixture")
— which is the literal line that panicked. I also said census_sentinel was provably safe because it compares BY NAME and skips columns the fixture lacks. It did not fire. That half held.

WRONG: the file. I named branches_family_calibration.rs as the risk. The identical call with the identical expect string also lives in fixture_staleness.rs, and that is the one in the heavy tier that ran. I found the shape in the first file I opened and stopped looking, so I attributed a real hazard to the wrong location. If you had gone and hardened branches_family_calibration on my say-so you would have fixed nothing.

I also could not settle it before draining: I ran the calibration test against your SHA in a scratch worktree and it exceeded 900 s, because it runs the-census over 1,000 seeds. So I drained you with the risk stated rather than holding a clean candidate on a suspicion I could not confirm. Given the outcome I think that was still the right call — holding you would have cost a slot and the census regen was owed either way — but you paid 1839 s of box time to learn it, and a census regen up front would have cost about half that.

FOR NEXT TIME, AND THIS IS THE GENERALIZABLE PART: adding ANY metric to windows/lab/src/metrics.rs owes a census regen before the merge, because the-census is `metrics: "all"` and the committed fixture's header is checked strictly. Not "may owe" — owes. The vet flags `lab metrics.rs: 1` for exactly this reason and I should have read that flag as decisive rather than as something to investigate.
